The Supreme Court has denied a last-minute request
from the Trump administration to wade into its unprecedented feud
with California over the state's voter rolls.
NPR's Jujampi Block reports that denial comes just hours
after the Justice Department filed its appeal.
The Justice Department wanted the high court
to force California election officials to set aside ballots
that pertain to 20,000 people that federal officials say
are likely non-citizens.
But California election officials and data experts
have argued the DOJ's list is full of errors.
Plus, they've said segregating ballots
isn't feasible with voting already underway.
The Supreme Court's refusal to take on the case
comes after both a federal judge and the Ninth Circuit Court
of Appeals rejected the DOJ's demand last week,
citing that the Constitution gives states
authority to run elections.
Plus, federal courts tend to avoid changing voting rules
right before an election.
Jujampi Block, NPR News.
On the eve of midterm election day,
the country seems polarized, but research and interviews
reveal a majority in the middle
who share views across partisan lines.
Here's NPR's Frank Langford.
Americans are reluctant to talk politics
because they want to avoid conflict.
But researchers say that can contribute
to people overestimating partisan differences
on issues ranging from immigration to racism.
Kristin Lauren is a professor of psychology
at the University of British Columbia.
Our perceived polarization far outstrips
are the actual polarization.
In fact, the nonpartisan Pew Research Center
classifies Americans into nine separate groups
based on values and attitudes.
Jocelyn Kiley is Pew's director of politics research.
Actually, this kind of messy political middle
is larger than those groups on the ideological right
and the ideological left.
Pew estimates the political middle
accounts for 60% of the population.
Frank Langford, NPR News.
Recent developments in mRNA vaccines
have shown promise fighting cancer.
NPR's Yuki Noguchi reports that researchers
are trying to figure out what's behind
some recent successful trials.
Seven years ago, Donna Gustafson
received the world's first mRNA vaccine
against pancreatic cancer.
I had no symptoms, no side effects to the point

But it has.
Gustafson has lived cancer free since.
The personalized vaccine used samples of her tumor
to genetically reprogram immune cells
to recognize distinctive proteins on her cancerous cells
and kill them.
Similar vaccines are being tested on lung, kidney, bladder,
and brain cancers.
But researchers don't yet understand
why some trials have failed, while others
are showing radical results.
Yuki Noguchi, NPR News.
And this is NPR News.
Federal safety investigators say the weather
will be a major focus of the investigation
into Sunday's crash of a business
jet in South Florida.
The National Transportation Safety Board
says rain pounded the region Sunday,

at a high altitude.
The NTSB said Monday that evidence found at the crash
site indicated the aircraft started to break up in the air.
Nine people were killed.

Both players have pleaded not guilty to charges of fraud,
sports, bribery, and money laundering.
If convicted, they face decades of prison time.
Becky Sullivan in "Pierre News."
A British man returned to his mother's home

Carl Buschby was a 29-year-old former paratrooper.
When he began the journey, he's now 57,
